concept.name: Morning doji star
concept.definition: A three-candlestick bottom reversal pattern: a long black body is followed by a doji that gaps below it (the doji star), and then a long white body that closes well into the first candle's real body. It is the morning star with a doji as the middle candle, conventionally regarded as a stronger reversal signal because the doji marks a more complete stall in selling.
concept.intuition: After heavy selling, the market opens lower but goes absolutely nowhere (a doji), then buyers storm back and reclaim most of the decline; the dead-flat middle candle shows sellers are spent.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long black body in a downtrend; candle 2 is a doji whose body (and classically whose range) sits below body 1; candle 3 is a long white body closing above the midpoint of body 1. When the doji also gaps away from both neighbors' shadows, the pattern becomes the rarer bullish abandoned baby.
concept.failure_modes: True gap-separated doji stars are rare in 24-hour markets, so relaxed versions are common and less reliable. Even textbook instances fail when the broader downtrend is powerful and the third candle lacks volume.
concept.misconceptions: It is not interchangeable with the plain morning star; the middle candle must be a doji. It is also distinct from the bullish abandoned baby, which additionally requires the doji's shadows to gap clear of both neighbors.
concept.example: A stock falls with a long black candle (35.00 to 33.00), then prints a doji near 32.60 after gapping down, then rallies on a long white candle closing at 34.50. The morning doji star is read as a strong bottom reversal signal.
